sentences.text: Upon raising cry, her husband came and rescue her.
The complaint was sent to concerned police station under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. and FIR was registered for offence under Section 341, 323, 376/511 IPC.
After investigation, the police submitted FR that no case is made out against the accused.
The petitioner filed a protest petition before the learned Special Judge, POCSO Act Cases, Jalore.

entities.text: Special Judge, POCSO Act Cases, Jalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: After considering the evidence collected during investigation and recording statement of witnesses, the court of learned Special Judge, POCSO Act Cases, Jalore accepted the Final Report and rejected the protest petition vide order dated 16.05.2019.

Learned Public Prosecutor and counsel for the respondents supported the impugned order and submitted that the trial court has discussed each and every aspect of the matter and have rightly rejected the protest petition, which does not called for any interference.
Heard the learned counsel for the respondents and perused the order impugned.

It is not disputed that after thorough investigation, the police submitted a final report to the effect that no case is made out against the accused respondent as the petitioner failed to make out a prima facie case against the accused respondent by adducing independent witnesses.

Learned trial court after [2024:RJ-JD:12168] (3 of 3) [CRLR-1054/2019] considering the Final report submitted by the police so also recording statements under Section 200 & 202 Cr.P.C, rejected the protest petition on the said ground by way of a detailed order.
In the opinion of this Court, no plausible ground exists for disbelieving the negative Final report filed by the police after thorough investigation.
Learned court below after considering the entire material on record, has accepted the Final report filed by the police.
There is no illegality or perversity in the impugned order dated 16.05.2019.
Hence, this revision petition is hereby dismissed.
Stay petition is also dismissed.

(MANOJ KUMAR GARG),J 161-BJSH/-
